_why: RUN TO COMPLETION 2026-08-15: 8 of 8 caught, in two invocations of four
rows each using `--only L1,L2,L3,L4` then `--only L5,L6,L7,L8`.
Parked as `.unverified` by its author because nine pytest invocations in
one command exceeded the per-call ceiling. `--only` splits the RUN
without splitting the record, which is what the flag was added for. The
ADR 0062's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
'Take out all code related to Tellurium' would delete the engine:
libRoadRunner (Apache 2.0, University of Washington) and Antimony (MIT)
underpin all fifteen domains. A licence IS permission; silence is not.
The four `@replit/*` packages that grant nothing were the real finding.
L5 is the row that escaped the original hand-run table. Reverting the
three-state licence detector passed all seven tests, because the only
when the detector finds nothing. The fix was to assert the POSITIVE
direction first: the detector must actually see the four it knows about.

mutations.description: an unlicensed package is re-imported into a vite config
mutations._note: A manifest entry is a paperwork problem; an import is a use. This is the row that would matter in a dispute, and it is why the call sites came out before the manifest entries could.
mutations.replace:
import path from "path";
import devBanner from "@replit/vite-plugin-dev-banner";

mutations.description: a NO_GRANT entry loses its reason
mutations._note: A prohibition nobody can evaluate gets removed by the next person who hits it.

mutations.description: libroadrunner is moved out of PERMISSION
mutations._note: Deleting this entry is a decision to delete the simulation engine. It should not be possible to make it by accident.

mutations.description: a PERMISSION entry names a licence but records no grant
mutations._note: The licence name is not the grant. 'MIT' tells a reader nothing about what they may do.
mutations.find: "numpy": ("BSD-3-Clause", "Use, modify and redistribute with the notice retained."),

mutations.description: 'installed and declares nothing' is conflated with 'not installed'
mutations._claimed: 1 failed (NOT caught before the positive assertion was added)
mutations._note: Three states, not two. Collapsing the last two accused autoprefixer -- plainly MIT, merely absent from this checkout -- of the same defect as the @replit packages. Reporting missing evidence as a finding is how a guard loses the credibility it needs on the day it is right.

mutations.description: the detector reports everything as unlicensed
mutations._note: The crying-wolf direction. A guard that flags 494 permissively-licensed packages gets switched off within the hour.

mutations.description: a recorded outstanding item goes back to blocking the whole suite
mutations._note: Added after the original table. This guard sat in `make guards` -- the documented pre-PR command -- exiting 1 over four packages a contributor could not remove without a pnpm lockfile regeneration, and make stops at the first failure. Blocking the suite on someone else's recorded item is not visibility, it is obstruction.
mutations.replace:
if blocking or unrecorded or outstanding:
        return 1

mutations.description: Rule 7 stops blocking and merely warns
mutations._note: Everything else in NO_GRANT is a removal someone has to schedule. `tellurium` is a prohibition, and a prohibition that only warns is a preference.
